source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Select "Hardware status" > Click tab "Inventory and LEDs" then check the DIMM information and detail information

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Data should be readable and correct.

original_test_intent: Unresolved: the preserved Items names processor inventory, while the preserved WebUI Procedure explicitly requests DIMM information and detail. Both are read-only inventory functions, but they target different components, schemas and acceptance matrices.
original_method: Do not execute a guessed target. Preserve the WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs path, determine whether the authoritative component is Processor, DIMM, or two separately required checkpoints, then define its complete member fields, present/absent/disabled semantics, topology/slot mapping, Project-spec comparison, protected API/UI evidence and redaction before collecting read-only inventory.
manual_activity: An engineer must first resolve the component identity and acceptance fields. After that decision, complete read-only inventory collection and normalization can be automated; optional WebUI visual correlation remains operator-reviewed and the final verdict remains engineer-owned.
required_inputs: Authoritative processor, DIMM or dual-checkpoint scope
Validated component-specific Redfish/UI resources and schema
safety_requirements: Do not choose Processor solely from the title or DIMM solely from the Procedure; preserve the conflict and wait for engineer scope.
Do not use `curl -k`, expose credentials, assume fixed `/Systems/system` paths or return only member names.
Run only read operations after the target decision; do not alter BIOS CPU/memory settings, power state, inventory records or logs.
Follow pagination and every member link; distinguish absent/disabled/unknown hardware from omitted or failed API responses.
Redact serial/asset data according to Project policy while keeping stable slot/socket identity and raw-to-normalized traceability.
Stop on wrong System resource, schema mismatch, duplicate/missing topology identity or incomplete collection; do not work around ambiguity with writes.
agent_execution_scope: Before decision, preserve the exact source conflict and collect no DUT evidence under an assumed target.
After engineer approval, validate the selected component resource/schema, protected access, expected population and field matrix.
Collect the complete paginated collection and all member records read-only, normalize topology/status and compare with the approved baseline.
Optionally correlate the exact WebUI detail view without any platform mutation.
Archive raw/redacted and normalized evidence and return facts without DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Decide whether this source identity owns Processor inventory, DIMM inventory, or two independently accepted checkpoints; correct the Review-layer purpose without modifying Master.
Approve the selected resource, topology/field/status matrix, expected Project baseline and redaction.
After reclassification, review complete inventory evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The processor GET fits only the Items interpretation and directly contradicts the DIMM Procedure. It also disables TLS verification, exposes credentials, assumes one URI and returns only names, so it is neither safe nor complete even if Processor is selected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No execution command is authorized until the component target is resolved. Then use protected schema-driven pagination for the approved Processor or Memory/DIMM collection and preserve the WebUI checkpoint/override coverage.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The misspelled Proccesor Items, DIMM-detail Procedure, generic Criteria, no Script/Bundle and 2/0-minute estimates remain exactly preserved; none is silently rewritten.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: After target resolution, collect complete component-specific member inventory over protected read-only Redfish and correlate the preserved WebUI detail view against Project SPEC.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Undetermined until Processor versus DIMM scope is decided.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, WebUI build and selected Redfish schema after decision.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor component inventory mapping plus Project hardware/recipe specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Would add complete protected collection, topology normalization and evidence discipline without deleting either conflicting Master statement.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Processor evidence cannot prove DIMM inventory and DIMM evidence cannot prove processor inventory; one branch must not be declared equivalent to both.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Target decision, resource/schema, field/topology matrix and expected baseline.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Executing the wrong branch yields credible-looking but irrelevant evidence and a false review conclusion.

project_override_considerations: An API can substitute for the WebUI only after the component target is decided and the original method, actual method, reason, engineer approval, field/topology equivalence and uncovered visual coverage are recorded. A different tool cannot resolve the Master identity conflict.
expected_evidence: Engineer decision establishing Processor, DIMM or separately accepted dual scope, with corrected Review-layer acceptance
BMC/WebUI/schema identity, trusted access and component-specific resource discovery
Complete raw redacted paginated collection and every member record for the approved target
Normalized socket/slot/population/model/capacity/status/health matrix and authoritative Project-spec comparison
Optional exact WebUI correlation, proof of no write/power/BIOS/log-clear action and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items says `Proccesor`, while Procedure says to check DIMM information and detail. Processor and DIMM are different hardware targets with different Redfish resources and acceptance fields; the generic Criteria cannot disambiguate them.

blocked_analysis.analysis: This is not merely a missing expected value: the core component under test is contradictory. Executing either branch would guess away preserved coverage, so the case remains BLOCKED until an engineer assigns authoritative or split scope.

review_improvement: Prevents a false PASS on the wrong component and makes the irreducible Processor-versus-DIMM ownership conflict explicit for engineering resolution.
independent_technical_reasoning: Processor inventory and DIMM inventory differ in identity, topology, population semantics, attributes and Redfish collections. Although both are harmless read-only checks, evidence for one is irrelevant to the other. Because the source gives one in Items and the other in Procedure, technical completeness requires an engineer decision before any command can be judged applicable.
